title: Root-projection reduction of finite ramified Tate coefficients
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $n\geq1$, and put $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. For any scheme $T$ on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-pc-scheme], work on $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$ with constant ring sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Put $Z_T=(\mathbf Z_\ell)_T$, $R_{r,T}=(\mathbf Z/\ell^r)_T$ and $L_T=\varprojlim_{s\geq1}\mu_{\ell^s,T}^{\mathrm{pro}}$, with root projections $p_{r,T}$ and power transitions $P_{r',r}:z\mapsto z^{\ell^{r'-r}}$ [def-pur-roots-of-unity-sheaf, def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit]. Let $P_T=A_T^{\mathrm{pro}}(1)$ be the prescribed finite pro-etale twist [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], and use sheaf tensors [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product].

There is a canonical reassociation isomorphism $j_T:P_T\xrightarrow{\sim}L_T\otimes_{Z_T}A_T$, taking $(x\otimes b)\otimes a$ to $x\otimes ba$. For every $r\geq1$ with $\ell^rA=0$, the map induced by $p_{r,T}$ is an isomorphism
$$\theta_{r,T}:P_T\xrightarrow{\sim}D_{r,T}:=\mu_{\ell^r,T}^{\mathrm{pro}}\otimes_{R_{r,T}}A_T,\qquad j_T^{-1}(x\otimes a)\longmapsto p_{r,T}(x)\otimes a.$$
For $r'\geq r$ with $\ell^rA=0$ it satisfies $(P_{r',r}\otimes1)\theta_{r',T}=\theta_{r,T}$; thus $P_{r',r}\otimes1:D_{r',T}\to D_{r,T}$ is invertible, and these maps obey the identity and composition equations.

For every scheme morphism $v:T'\to T$, use pro-etale inverse image [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], identifying inverse images of constant rings with the target constant rings. Let $c^v_s:v^{-1}\mu_{\ell^s,T}^{\mathrm{pro}}\to\mu_{\ell^s,T'}^{\mathrm{pro}}$ be the canonical root map adjoint to pullback of units [def-pur-roots-of-unity-inverse-image]. There is a unique map $c^v_L:v^{-1}L_T\to L_{T'}$ with $p_{s,T'}c^v_L=c^v_sv^{-1}p_{s,T}$ for all $s$. Define $b_v:v^*P_T\to P_{T'}$ by transporting $c^v_L\otimes1$ through $j_T,j_{T'}$ and the canonical tensor pullback identifications. Then
$$\theta_{r,T'}b_v=(c^v_r\otimes1)v^*\theta_{r,T}.$$
The maps $c^v_L,b_v$ obey the identity and composition laws under the canonical inverse-image identifications. These assertions concern ordinary tensor products and require only $\ell^rA=0$, with no flatness of $A$ over $\mathbf Z/\ell^r$ and no ramification-index divisibility condition.

proof.text: Apply [lem-amb-root-tower-finite-tensor] with $B=A$. It gives locally surjective root projections, their shift-kernel description, and the normalized isomorphism $\alpha_{r,T}:L_T\otimes_{Z_T}A_T\xrightarrow{\sim}D_{r,T}$. The hypotheses hold because $A$ is a commutative $\mathbf Z_\ell$-algebra and $\ell^rA=0$. Set $\theta_{r,T}=\alpha_{r,T}j_T$. Its pure-tensor formula is the one asserted, including the inverse prescribed by local root lifts. In Lean apply the theorem to ULift A to match its coefficient universe, identify the scalar maps by functoriality of constant sheaves and uniqueness of ring homomorphisms from ZMod, and transport the normalized existence statement. Pure scalar-extension tensors determine the chosen isomorphism uniquely.

proof.text: Define the transition D_s to D_r as alpha_s inverse followed by alpha_r. To check the required power-map formula on a tensor a tensor x, use local surjectivity of p_s to lift x locally to a root-limit section y. There the formula follows from alpha normalization and p_s followed by the tower power map equalling p_r. The arbitrary tower map has exponent l^(s-r): prove this by induction from the successor maps using the kernel inclusion into units. Separatedness glues the section equality. The transition-theta equation, invertibility, identity, and composition are then the isomorphism cancellation identities.

source.place: Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product; defining power-transition formula in def-pur-roots-of-unity-sheaf

proof.text: Apply [lem-amb-root-tower-pullback-coherence] with $B=A$. This gives the unique specified $c^v_L$, its identity/composition laws, and $h_v$ on $H_T=L_T\otimes_{Z_T}A_T$ with $\alpha_{r,T\prime}h_v=(c^v_r\otimes1)v^*\alpha_{r,T}$. Define $b_v=j_{T\prime}^{-1}h_v(v^*j_T)$. Substitute $\theta=\alpha j$ to get $\theta_{r,T\prime}b_v=(c^v_r\otimes1)v^*\theta_{r,T}$. In the identity and composite expressions for $b$, the adjacent $v^*j$ and its inverse cancel; the corresponding laws for $h$ give precisely the asserted laws for $b$. On the empty scheme these are unique maps of zero sheaves. The two new results use ordinary tensors, and the only annihilation hypothesis in the finite comparison is $\ell^rA=0$. Identify the coherence theorem projection map with the finite normalized isomorphism using scalar-extension hom extensionality. Constant-ring naturality under the specified direct-image adjuncts follows from the sheafification adjunction and naturality of its unit. This proves the integral quotient compatibility needed for the double pure tensor formula. All transports are isomorphisms with specified pure-tensor normalizations.
